title: Mateo is 8 months old and fighting stage four cancer
story:
Little Mateo is facing a battle that no child should ever have to live through. He is only 8 months old and has been diagnosed with stage four cancer. His world — and that of his entire family — changed overnight.

Instead of a normal childhood, full of laughter and discovery, Mateo's days now pass in hospitals, surrounded by doctors, treatments, and constant uncertainty.

His cancer treatment requires intensive chemotherapy, high-cost medications, continuous hospitalizations, and transfers to specialized centers. Each session is another step in his fight, but it also represents an enormous financial burden for his family.

Doctors have scheduled new phases of treatment. For these to take place without delay, the family needs to raise the funds in time. Every day that passes without resources could mean an interruption in his recovery.

Mateo's family cannot cover the chemotherapy, medications, clinical studies, hospitalizations, and transfers on their own. Your help can allow him to complete every phase of treatment without further interruptions.

The original campaign reported 10,360,000 MXN raised out of a goal of 18,500,000 MXN. For this international presentation, both figures were converted to US dollars using the European Central Bank's reference rate from September 10, 2026.

Any donation, no matter how small, can bring Mateo closer to the complete treatment he needs. If you cannot donate, sharing his story can also help enormously.

title: Urgent Help Needed for Graceline's Second Bone Marrow Transplant
story:
My name is Gema. I am writing as a mother standing on the edge of losing everything our family holds dear. Our beautiful 12-year-old daughter, Graceline Bennett, received the devastating news that her cancer has returned during her fifth cycle of maintenance chemotherapy.

The latest bone marrow aspiration results showed a 4.8% increase in leukemia cells. The previous Donor Lymphocyte Infusion and maintenance chemotherapy were unable to stop the aggressive growth. Her medical team says she must undergo two more cycles of intensive chemotherapy immediately, followed by a second bone marrow transplant.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-graceline-now/story-01.jpg|Graceline's medical journey

In less than one year, our little girl may have to endure two highly complex bone marrow transplants. We need to raise the cost of the second transplant while also living with the fear that her exhausted body may not survive it.

The Agony of Relapse

On May 20, 2026, Graceline began her first cycle of intensive chemotherapy after this heartbreaking relapse. Doctors placed a PICC line directly into her arm to administer the drugs needed to suppress the Acute Myeloid Leukemia cells. When the anesthesia wore off, the pain was sharp and overwhelming. Even the slightest touch near the line sent pain through her body.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-graceline-now/story-02.jpg|Graceline with her family

We pray that every stage of treatment goes smoothly and that she is given strength, patience, and moments of joy. She is incredibly tired, yet she continues to fight with everything she has because she knows she is our only remaining child.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-graceline-now/story-03.jpg|Graceline during treatment

A Grief We Cannot Fully Mourn

Two years ago, while we were already fighting for Graceline through intensive chemotherapy, another tragedy shattered our family. Her younger brother Sean contracted meningitis. His illness moved so quickly that while we were trying to save our daughter, our son quietly slipped away from us. We buried our baby boy while Graceline was still fighting for her life in the hospital.

There is a particular silence in a home that has lost a child. We could not collapse or mourn Sean the way he deserved because Graceline still needed us. We dried our tears, put our masks back on, and returned to the oncology ward.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-graceline-now/story-04.jpg|Family moments with Graceline

A Fleeting Victory

For a short time, we believed the cancer had been beaten. In April 2025, her symptoms returned with a sudden fever, a dangerously low platelet count, and rising blast cells. We rushed her to a hospital in Singapore, where doctors said she needed intensive chemotherapy followed by a bone marrow transplant.

On July 25, doctors told us her blast cells were negative and she was ready for transplant. In September 2025, Graceline completed her first bone marrow transplant. It was a tremendous victory, but that transplant alone cost approximately $300,000.

After the critical 100-day milestone, she needed maintenance chemotherapy to prevent another relapse. The cost reached nearly $20,000 each month for medicine and blood tests. Her immune system remained dangerously weak, and the planned six maintenance cycles were eventually increased to eight.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-graceline-now/story-05.jpg|Hope during recovery

Back to the Starting Line

On April 13, another bone marrow test brought the news we feared most: the cancer had returned. Most families worry about school grades and scraped knees. We worry about white blood cell counts, painful catheters, and invisible cancer cells in our daughter's blood.

Graceline should be thinking about homework and friends. Instead, she faces chemotherapy side effects and the terrifying possibility of another transplant. I see the future she deserves, and I cannot let the same shadow that took Sean take her away too.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-graceline-now/story-06.jpg|Graceline needs urgent help

We Urgently Need Your Help

To save her life, doctors must perform intensive chemotherapy, a Donor Lymphocyte Infusion, and the second bone marrow transplant as soon as possible. The estimated total for this new phase is $363,700.

We have nothing left to sell and nowhere left to borrow from. We are humbly asking for help to cross this finish line. Every donation supports Graceline's immediate chemotherapy, medical care, and second transplant. Thank you for keeping our daughter in your prayers and standing with our family.

title: Make a donation to ease Fabi's severe pain and help save her life!
story:

title: Save Jazzy's life from brain cancer & being homeless
story:
Jazzy has been battling Neuroblastoma cancer for over 7 years. After years of treatments, surgeries, hospital stays, pain, and setbacks, her family is now desperately searching for the next option that could help save her life.

Jazzy’s cancer has now spread throughout her body, including her spine, arms, and brain. In the past two months alone, she has endured three major brain surgeries, had three tumors removed from her head, and doctors have recently found new bumps appearing across her body. She is also currently relearning how to walk.

They have spent every last penny they have to the point they are currently homeless.

Despite everything she has been through, Jazzy is still fighting with so much strength, courage, and hope.

Right now, Jazzy is running out of options, and her family is searching for clinical trials and specialized treatments that may give her another chance.

Her family is doing everything possible to get her to a clinical trial and specialized treatment in Rome, Italy, along with any additional cancer treatments that could help save her life. The treatment starts at around $350,000 USD- a number they can only dream to achieve to possibly save her life.

Because of Jazzy’s extensive treatment needs, her family is currently unable to work. On top of medical costs and travel, they are also caring for their other children back home while trying to stay by Jazzy’s side through this fight.

Jazzy has been fighting for her life since she was a little girl. She has been through more than any child should ever have to face, but she is still here, still smiling, still hoping, and still fighting.

Thank you so much to everyone who loves, supports, prays for, and believes in Jazzy. Your kindness means more than words can ever explain.

title: Help 5-year-old Teddy Beat Brain Cancer
story:
Hi, we're Cindy and Liam, and we're raising funds for our son, Teddy.

Just a few months before his fifth birthday, Teddy was a happy little boy enjoying everything childhood should be about — playing, laughing and making memories with his family.

Nothing could have prepared us for how suddenly our lives were about to change.

After becoming unwell, Teddy underwent a CT scan and we received the devastating news that he needed emergency brain surgery for a mass at the back of his brain.

Following surgery, we were told every parent's worst nightmare.

Teddy had metastatic medulloblastoma, a Grade 4 pediatric brain cancer with MYC amplification — one of the most aggressive forms of childhood brain cancer. By the time it was discovered, the disease had already spread throughout his brain, spine and cerebrospinal fluid.

Since that day, our family has been living a reality we never imagined possible.

Teddy has faced brain surgery, intensive treatment, countless hospital visits, scans, tests and procedures that no child should ever have to endure. Through every setback, he has continued to show a strength that inspires everyone around him.

Today, we find ourselves facing the most important challenge of Teddy's journey so far. Despite everything he has been through, there is still hope.

Teddy has been provisionally accepted into a pioneering clinical trial at Penn State Children's Hospital in Pennsylvania, USA. The trial uses DFMO therapy and has shown promising results in helping children with high-risk medulloblastoma remain in remission.

For the first time since Teddy's diagnosis, we have been given a genuine opportunity to fight for a future beyond this disease.

But there is one devastating obstacle: we have just 60 days to get Teddy to the United States and secure his place in the programme. After that, the opportunity may no longer be available to him.

The cost of treatment, medical monitoring, travel, accommodation and insurance is estimated to exceed $250,000 — far beyond what our family can raise alone.

We understand that no treatment comes with guarantees. But we cannot walk away from a chance that could help keep Teddy's cancer from returning. If Teddy's cancer relapses, his chances of survival become heartbreakingly low.

That is why we are asking for your help today.

Every donation will help give Teddy the opportunity to access this potentially life-saving treatment and the future every five-year-old deserves.

If you are unable to donate, sharing Teddy's story could be just as powerful and may help us reach someone who can.

Thank you for taking the time to read Teddy's story, for standing beside our family and for helping us fight for his future.

With love and gratitude,
Cindy, Liam and Teddy

title: Help Daniel Get a Life-Saving Liver Transplant
story:
My name is Daniel, and in 2024 I was diagnosed with liver cancer.

It was not caused by an unhealthy lifestyle, but by a dormant hepatitis B infection that was passed from my mother to me at birth.

I have been through multiple liver surgeries, chemotherapy, local treatments and fifteen cycles of immunotherapy. Unfortunately, despite all of these treatments, the cancer keeps coming back aggressively.

Today, a living-donor liver transplant is my only chance of a cure. My latest scan showed a new aggressive tumour, but the good news is that there is no evidence the cancer has spread outside the liver. If it spreads beyond the liver, a transplant will no longer be an option and a cure may no longer be possible.

The transplant process in the Netherlands is taking longer than my doctors and I can safely afford because of how aggressively the cancer is recurring. I am sitting on a ticking time bomb and cannot wait until the process finally catches up with the urgency of my illness.

After carefully reviewing every option with my medical team, I decided to move forward with the transplant process in Turkey. My hospital in the Netherlands is already working with Turkish doctors, and this route allows us to move much faster while the transplant is still clinically viable. Unfortunately, the treatment is not covered by my health insurance.

Anyone who knows me knows that I have always believed that if something in my life needed fixing, it was my responsibility to find a solution. I never liked asking for help, especially when it came to money. I have come to realize that taking responsibility now does not mean trying to do everything alone. It means doing everything within my power to survive, even if that means setting my pride aside and asking for help.

The goal of this fundraiser is $114,000. The money will be used for:

• Transplant surgery.

• Donor surgery and medical evaluation.

• Hospitalisation and medication.

• Travel and accommodation.

• Medical follow-up, recovery and a reserve for unexpected complications.

The donor does not receive any payment. The costs cover the donor's medical evaluation, surgery, hospitalisation and post-operative follow-up.

Everyone who donates deserves full transparency. I will continue sharing updates throughout this process.

If you decide to donate, thank you. If donating is not possible, sharing this page with others can make an enormous difference.

Thank you for giving me a second chance at a wonderful life.

With love,

Daniel

title: Help Save My Daughter Vexanna
story:
My name is Maria, and I am Vexanna's mother.

I never imagined I would have to share my daughter's pain with the world to ask for help. As a mother, all I have ever wanted was to protect her. Today, I can no longer do it alone.

Vexanna was born with a rare condition called hydrocephalus, a disease that causes cerebrospinal fluid to build up inside the brain, creating dangerous pressure and causing her head to grow much larger than normal. From the day she was born, our lives became filled with hospitals, medical appointments, surgeries, fear, and uncertainty.

When she was only 2 years old, our lives changed forever.

One night, while she was sleeping, the pressure inside her head became so severe that the fragile tissue covering her skull ruptured. I will never forget waking up to that nightmare.

Fluid from the wound began to leak, and before I realized what was happening, ants had entered our room and started crawling onto my baby's head. Seeing my little girl in that condition is something no mother should ever have to experience.

That moment broke my heart forever.

Since that day, Vexanna has lived with an extremely fragile skull. Today, part of her head has little to no protective bone covering it. Instead of feeling hard like a normal skull, that area feels soft and incredibly delicate. Even the smallest bump or accidental touch could cause a devastating injury.

We live every single day in fear.

Hydrocephalus is much more than having an enlarged head. It can lead to seizures, severe headaches, vision loss, developmental delays, infections, mobility problems, and permanent brain damage if left untreated. Every day is a battle to keep my daughter safe.

Vexanna depends on me for absolutely everything.

Because of her condition, I cannot work. She needs constant supervision and care 24 hours a day. My days are spent taking her to medical appointments, giving her medications, caring for her delicate head, and doing everything I can to keep her alive.

While I care for my daughter, our bills continue to grow.

We struggle to afford food, rent, electricity, transportation, medications, medical appointments, examinations, and the daily supplies she desperately needs.

I never imagined I would have to ask strangers for help.

But when I look into my daughter's eyes and see her still smiling despite everything she has endured, I know I cannot give up.

If you can make a donation, no matter how small, you will be helping us continue Vexanna's treatment, provide the care she desperately needs, and give her the chance to live a safer and more dignified life.

And if you are unable to donate, simply sharing our story means more than you could ever imagine.

Thank you for opening your heart to my little girl.

May God bless you and your family.

With all my love and gratitude,

Maria, Vexanna's Mom

title: Help Olivia Live with Dignity
story:
My name is Olivia. I am 19 years old, and I live with muscular dystrophy.

Little by little, this disease has taken away my ability to move. Today, I cannot walk, get out of bed on my own, or do even the simplest daily tasks. My wheelchair and my bed are where I spend almost my entire life.

But there is one person who has never left my side.

My mom.

She has devoted her entire life to taking care of me. Every morning she lifts me out of bed and into my wheelchair. She helps me bathe, get dressed, eat, and takes care of all my daily needs. She is the one who takes me to every doctor’s appointment, every medical exam, and every treatment. She is with me every hour of every day.

She isn’t just my mother.

She is my caregiver, my strength, my best friend, and the reason I keep smiling through all of this.

The hardest part is knowing how much she has sacrificed for me.

Because I depend on her for absolutely everything, she cannot have a job. She has spent nearly two decades caring for me 24 hours a day. While others are able to build careers and plan their futures, my mom spends every day lifting me, helping me change positions, caring for our home, arranging my treatments, and making sure I have everything I need.

She has given me her entire life without ever asking for anything in return.

But love doesn’t pay the bills.

Today we are struggling just to cover our basic household expenses. Watching my mom worry about how we will make it through another month breaks my heart, because I know she already carries more than anyone should.

The wheelchair I use today is the same one I have had for 18 years.

It has worn out over time and no longer provides the support and safety my body needs. As my muscular dystrophy progresses, sitting for long periods becomes more painful, and transferring me becomes harder for my mom. A new wheelchair would not only improve my comfort—it would make my daily life safer and reduce the physical strain on the woman who cares for me every single day.

We also desperately need an accessible van.

For many people, transportation is something they never think about. For us, every hospital visit, every medical appointment, and every treatment is a major challenge. My mom has to struggle every time she moves me because we don’t have a vehicle designed for someone in my condition.

An accessible van would change our lives. It would allow me to travel safely and make every trip much easier for my mom, who has carried this responsibility almost entirely on her own for 19 years.

Muscular dystrophy is a progressive disease. My muscles continue to weaken, and my dependence grows with each passing year. I cannot change that reality, but I still hope for a life with a little more comfort, dignity, and less suffering for my mother.

I am not asking for luxury.

I am asking for the chance to make life a little easier for the woman who has sacrificed everything for me, and for the opportunity to continue receiving the medical care I need.

If you can donate or simply share my story, you will be helping not only me, but also the incredible mother who has never stopped fighting for her daughter.

Thank you for taking the time to read my story.

May God bless you and your family.

title: Help Save Sarah Collins: Her Only Chance Is a Second Stem Cell Transplant

This second stem cell transplant is not just another treatment—it is my best and only hope of beating this disease. Every day that passes without treatment gives the cancer more time to progress and reduces my chances of recovery.

My family and I are doing everything we can to raise the funds needed to move forward with this life-saving transplant. Unfortunately, the cost is far beyond what we could ever afford on our own.

I never thought I would have to ask for help again, but today I have no other choice. If you are able to donate, share my story, or keep me in your prayers, you will be giving me something priceless—another chance at life.

title: Help Ross Access Critical Cancer Treatment
story:
To my lovely supporters, old and new, I wanted to update you on how my week has been.

I was discharged from the Ron Johnson Ward on Monday after spending time there fighting two infections and taking a break from chemotherapy for one cycle. That gave me a genuinely lovely week at home, recovering and rebuilding not only my strength but also my confidence, which has been tested recently.

Monday was my seventh wedding anniversary, so we went out for dinner to celebrate. During the week, I visited Richmond Park with Stanley, my dog, and spent some time in nature. It was calming and restorative in a way I truly needed.

On Saturday, I celebrated a friend's birthday and got dressed up for dinner at his house. On Sunday, I visited Bournemouth, my hometown, to see my mum, dad and extended family. It was the first time I had been back since my diagnosis.

There were many positive moments in one week, and they reminded me exactly what this fight is worth. Throughout all of it, I have been taking care of myself, saving the energy I have for the things that matter most and resting whenever needed.

Now I have until Thursday to prepare for my next round of treatment — full power this time.

Thank you, as always, for standing with me through this. Your support is helping me continue fighting for access to the cancer treatment I urgently need.

title: Help Cristian Navarro Keep Fighting for His Life
story:
My name is Rosa and I am Cristian Navarro's grandmother. Today I find myself forced to ask for help because I no longer have the strength to keep facing this fight alone.

I never imagined that, at my age, I would have to ask for help to keep my grandson alive. But life put us in front of a test no family should have to live through.

Cristian was diagnosed with a malignant tumor in the rectum, a very aggressive type of cancer that requires constant treatment, medications, medical studies, and specialized care. The disease causes him severe pain, great physical wear, extreme weakness, and many difficulties moving. Today he needs to use diapers, depends on help for most of his daily activities, and also needs a wheelchair to be able to get around with a little more dignity and safety.

But Cristian's pain is not only physical.

A few years ago we lost my daughter, his mother, in a tragic traffic accident. It was a blow that shattered our whole family. Shortly after, when Cristian's father learned that his son had cancer, he decided to abandon him. He never came back. He never sent money, never asked how he was doing, never offered a single word of support.

As if that weren't enough, Cristian's girlfriend also left him when he needed her most.

Imagine the pain of a young man who has lost his mother, was abandoned by his father and by the person he loved, while fighting a cancer that puts his life at risk every day. Little by little he stopped smiling, and today he also faces deep depression caused by so much suffering, loneliness, and abandonment.

I am the one who takes care of Cristian.

But I am also an older woman.

My husband, Cristian's grandfather, is diabetic and also needs daily care. I spend 24 hours a day looking after both of them, administering medications, helping them with everything they need, and trying to keep them hopeful. Because of this situation I can no longer work, and our income is not enough to cover even the most basic needs of our home.

Every month we struggle to get money for medications, diapers, food, medical studies, transportation to hospitals, and everything Cristian needs to continue his treatment. Many times I have to choose which need to address first, and that is a decision that breaks my heart.

I write these words with tears in my eyes because my greatest fear is not being able to give my grandson the chance to keep fighting for his life.

If you can help us with any donation, no matter how small, you will be giving hope to a young man who has suffered more than anyone should have to bear. And if you cannot contribute financially, I ask you with all my heart to share our story.

May God bless everyone who takes a few minutes to read this message and reach out a hand to our family.

With all my gratitude,

Rosa, Cristian Navarro's grandmother

story:

Every single day, her family must spend hours carefully changing bandages and treating her wounds to prevent dangerous infections. Without this care, the consequences can be devastating.

But there is hope.

With proper treatment, specialized bandages, and ongoing medical care, it is possible to ease her suffering and give Mark’s something every child deserves: a chance to live with less pain and more dignity.

The problem is that these treatments are extremely expensive. And that’s why we are asking for your help.

Yet every single day, Goyito wakes up and goes to work — not to beg, but to survive.

Because he cannot walk, Goyito must crawl on the ground to move from place to place. This is the only way he can work, collect recyclable materials, and earn a few dollars a day.

title: My Husband Doesn't Want to Die. He Just Wants to Live to See Our Son Grow Up.
story:
My name is Ana Rodríguez, and today I write these words with my heart completely shattered.

My husband, Ricardo Castillo, was diagnosed with colon cancer, an aggressive disease that develops in the large intestine and that, little by little, is consuming not only his body, but also the hope of an entire family.

Our life changed completely.

The strong, hardworking man full of dreams who always held up our home is today extremely weakened. The cancer and the treatments have left Ricardo very weak. He has lost a lot of weight, lives with constant pain, can barely eat, spends most of his time lying down, and has less strength every day to get out of bed. On top of that, the treatments cause him nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, extreme fatigue, and a weakness that keeps him from doing even the simplest activities.

Despite all the suffering he faces, there is a phrase he repeats every day while looking at our little son:

"I don't want to die… I just want to live to see my son grow up."

There is no greater pain for a wife than hearing those words and not knowing how to ease that fear.

Ricardo can no longer work because of his illness. And I can't either, because I must care for him 24 hours a day. He depends on me to take his medications, to help him get up, to go with him to his appointments, and to be by his side through every moment of this difficult battle.

Our only priority now is to fight for his life.

Without income, our situation has become desperate. Beyond the costs of appointments, tests, medications, special diets, and transportation for his treatments, today it is also hard for us to buy food and cover the most basic needs of our little son.

I never imagined I would have to ask for help publicly, but today we have no other option.

If you can make a donation, no matter the amount, you will be helping Ricardo continue his treatment, be able to access the medications he needs, and ensure our son has the essentials while we keep fighting to hold our family together.

And if you cannot help financially right now, I ask you with all my heart to share our story. Perhaps it will reach someone who can give us a chance to move forward.

On behalf of my husband Ricardo, our son, and our whole family, thank you for taking the time to read our story.

May God bless your life and your family's.

title: I Am Lucía Fernández. I Never Imagined I Would One Day Have to Ask for Help to Save the Man I Love.
story:
My name is Lucía Fernández and today I write with my heart completely shattered.

My husband, Armando, was always the pillar of our home. He was the one who went out to work every day, who fought to make sure food was never missing from our table, and who did everything possible to care for our family. He was always a strong, hardworking man full of hope.

But illness changed our lives completely.

His liver is severely damaged and no longer functions as it should. Every day I watch the man I love suffer intense pain throughout his whole body. His abdomen stays very swollen because of the disease, he lives with extreme exhaustion, and many times he can't even get out of bed.

As if that weren't enough, Armando also suffers from a serious throat problem that prevents him from eating normally. Every bite has become a moment of pain. Watching the person you love suffer even to swallow a bit of food is something that breaks your heart.

He also suffers from inflammation of the colon, which causes him even more pain and completely limits his quality of life.

Today my husband can no longer walk on his own. He needs a wheelchair to attend his medical appointments, undergo tests, and even move around inside our own house. Little by little he has lost his independence and now depends on me for almost everything.

I also had to leave my job to care for him 24 hours a day. I cannot leave him alone for even a moment. This means our family is left with no income at all, right when expenses have become higher than ever.

The medications he needs are very expensive. In addition, Armando uses three packs of diapers every week and needs a special cream to protect his skin, along with medical appointments, tests, proper nutrition, and all the care his illness requires. Every week a new expense appears, and unfortunately, we no longer have a way to cover it.

I never thought I would have to ask for help from people I don't know. We always worked hard and with dignity to get ahead. But today we are not asking for luxuries; we are only asking for a chance for Armando to continue his treatment and live with a little less pain.

Any donation, no matter how small, will help us buy his medications, the diapers, the special cream, the wheelchair he needs so much, and cover the basic expenses of our home while we keep fighting this illness.

And if you cannot donate right now, I ask you with all my heart to share our story. Perhaps it will reach the right person and change our family's fate.

On behalf of Armando and our entire family, thank you for taking the time to read our story. May God deeply bless everyone who decides to reach out a hand to us in this very difficult moment.

title: Help Save My Son Thiago's Life
story:
My name is Lourdes Jesús, and writing these words is one of the hardest things I have ever had to do in my entire life.

I never imagined I would have to ask strangers for help to try to save my son.

Thiago is only 7 years old. He should be running, playing, going to school, and enjoying the childhood every child deserves. But instead, he spends his days in hospitals, among tests, needles, and chemotherapy sessions, fighting a devastating disease called Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL).

Leukemia is a cancer that affects the bone marrow and prevents the body from producing healthy blood cells. As a result, his body loses the ability to fight infections, carry oxygen, and control bleeding. A simple cold can put his life at risk.

Every day I watch my little boy suffer.

The chemotherapy is extremely aggressive. It causes him severe pain, unbearable exhaustion, constant nausea, vomiting, fever, hair loss, and a weakness so intense that many times he can't even get out of bed. There are days when he cannot eat, play, or even smile.

There is no greater pain for a mother than hearing her son beg for the pain to stop and not being able to do anything to ease it.

Since we received the diagnosis, I had to stop working to care for him 24 hours a day. Thiago depends on me completely. I go with him to every appointment, every hospitalization, and every treatment. I cannot leave him alone for even a moment.

That means we have no source of income today.

While we fight to save my son's life, we also face another battle: covering the most basic needs of our home. We need help buying food, medications, paying for transportation to the hospital, rent, utilities, and everything necessary to keep going.

Medical expenses are enormous and keep increasing. Many times I wonder how I am going to get the money for the next treatment, or simply to put a plate of food on the table.

Despite all the pain he faces, Thiago is still a child full of dreams. He asks me when he will be able to run again, play with other children, and live a normal childhood.

I keep believing that day will come.

But I cannot fight this battle alone.

Today, with all the humility in my heart, I ask you to help us. Any donation, no matter how small, brings us a little closer to hope. Your support will allow us to continue Thiago's treatment, buy his medications, cover transportation to the hospital, and sustain our family's basic needs while we keep fighting for his life.

And if you cannot donate right now, please share our story. A simple gesture can reach the right person and become the miracle we so badly need.

From one mother to another, from one father to another, from heart to heart…

Please help us give my son the chance to keep living.

May God bless everyone who decides to reach out a hand to us.

With all my love and eternal gratitude,

Lourdes Jesús

Thiago's Mom. ❤️

title: Help save Castiel’s life fighting Stage 4 Cancer
story:
Castiel is joy personified. He’s bright-eyed, full of giggles, cuddly beyond measure—the kind of baby who reaches out for you and instantly steals your heart. He is the light of his parents’ lives. He is also adored deeply by his big brother, Nicollas—a sweet, gentle 13-year-old on the autism spectrum. Just recently, Mike and Leidiane noticed a bump on Castiel’s head. Then another on his neck. Concerned, they brought him in for an ultrasound. They waited two agonizing days for that appointment. Within an hour of leaving that office came the call that turned their world upside down: “Take him to Children’s Hospital—immediately.” Castiel has been diagnosed with Stage Four High-Risk Neuroblastoma. Dozens of tumors have been found throughout his tiny body—his spine, kidneys, lungs, skull, neck, and bones. He is only a baby, but he is already in the fight of his life. Since his diagnosis, Castiel has endured more than any child should: • His first full five-day round of chemotherapy• A bone marrow extraction• Two blood transfusions• Multiple biopsies He’s only at the beginning of what will be an aggressive and invasive treatment plan: more transfusions, scans, surgeries, radiation, and ongoing chemo lie ahead. His body is already reacting—he’s in pain, with sores in his mouth, fighting through side effects he can’t possibly understand. He’s also teething right now—a cruel reminder of the milestones he should be reaching, of the baby life he should be living. Mike and Leidiane are also doing everything they can to support Nicollas, who thrives with consistency, routine, and close attention. Ensuring he feels safe and cared for during this time is just as essential—and presents an added layer of emotional and logistical challenge as they navigate hospital visits, appointments, and long days away from home. Nicollas and Castiel’s parents are kind, humble, and giving to the core. If you know them, you know this. If you don’t, just know that the love they pour into others is now being poured into their boys—with every ounce of strength they have. We’re raising funds to help cover:

️Extensive medical expenses not covered by insurance

️ Travel, parking, and lodging for hospital visits

️ Meals and daily expenses during extended stays

️Lost income, as both parents must miss work

️ Childcare and support for Nicollas No family is prepared for this. But we believe in the strength of community to carry a family through what no one should face alone. If you can give—please, do. Every dollar counts. If you can’t, please share. And above all, hold this family in your heart and prayers. Castiel is a warrior in footie pajamas. He’s fighting. So we will, too—beside him, for him, and with unshakable hope. Thank you for standing with Castiel.With love and gratitude.

title: Help Hilary Fight a Rare Cancer Relapse
story:
Hilary is only eight years old. After more than a year of treatment for an extremely rare cancer, she had to undergo the amputation of her right arm and part of her shoulder to stop the disease from advancing and protect her life.

About Her Name

In Brazilian public reporting, she is known as Áurea. For international outreach, this campaign uses the name Hilary to help protect her privacy. Both names refer to the same brave child and the same medical journey.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-hilary/story-g1-01.jpg|Hilary has kept smiling through hospital stays, procedures and treatment. Photo: Family archive, as published by G1 Santos.

How Her Fight Began

Her family's fight began in April 2025, when they noticed a lump near her right elbow. An MRI revealed a tumor. After further examinations and biopsies at GRAACC, a children's cancer hospital in São Paulo, doctors identified PEComa — a rare tumor that develops from cells associated with blood vessels.

Hilary endured six cycles of chemotherapy and three surgeries. For a brief moment, her family believed the cancer was gone. They celebrated the news and tried to give her the childhood moments treatment had taken away.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-hilary/story-g1-02.jpg|Even during treatment, Hilary continued finding moments to play, smile and enjoy being a child. Photo: Family archive, as published by G1 Santos.

When the Cancer Returned

Only a few months later, the cancer returned in a more aggressive form. The tumor appeared near her armpit and again close to the elbow. Doctors tried two cycles of intensive ICE chemotherapy and later returned to the original treatment protocol, but the disease continued to progress.

Her medical team explained that removing her right arm and part of her shoulder offered the best chance to save her life. The surgery took place on July 20. According to her family, the first pathology report found no disease in nine removed lymph nodes, but she still needs close monitoring and further examinations.

When her family explained what the surgery meant, Hilary responded with extraordinary courage: she understood that it was being done so she could stay alive and get well.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-hilary/story-g1-03.jpg|Hilary's journey before and after surgery shows the courage she carries into every stage of treatment. Photo: Family archive, as published by G1 Santos.

Her New Dream: Independence

Hilary continues taking chemotherapy tablets at home every day. She returns to GRAACC every seven to fifteen days for medical follow-up, blood tests and care for her PICC line. Through all of this, her family says she keeps smiling, playing and going to school whenever she can.

Now her greatest dream is a prosthetic arm. She wants more independence for the simple things children do every day — playing, getting dressed, studying and moving through life with greater freedom. The cost of the prosthesis is beyond what her family can manage alone.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-hilary/story-g1-04.jpg|Behind every hospital visit is an eight-year-old girl who loves color, play and moments of normal childhood. Photo: Family archive, as published by G1 Santos.

How Your Support Helps

The campaign's $40,000 goal will help the family pursue a suitable prosthesis while meeting the ongoing costs of treatment, medical follow-up, medication, transportation and daily care. The campaign has raised $24,000, leaving $16,000 to reach that goal.

Every contribution can bring Hilary closer to greater independence and give her family breathing room while they remain focused on her recovery. If you cannot donate, sharing her story can help it reach someone who can.

Thank you for standing beside Hilary and her family.

Story information reported by G1 Santos on August 11, 2026. Photos: Family archive, as published by G1 Santos.

I was born with a rare condition called *Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB)*, often known as Butterfly Skin Disease. My skin is so fragile that even the gentlest touch, a hug, or the friction from my clothes can tear it open and create new wounds. Every movement can be painful. Pain has been part of my life for as long as I can remember.

Besides the constant pain, this disease puts me at a high risk of serious infections, causes wounds that take a long time to heal, makes eating difficult because of painful sores, and requires continuous medical care. Pain medication, special non-stick bandages, wound care supplies, doctor visits, and nutritional support are all essential for me to keep fighting.

My family does everything they can to care for me, but we simply cannot afford the cost of my treatment anymore. Every month the expenses grow, and sometimes we are forced to choose between buying the medical supplies I need or paying for our basic household necessities.

I have been too ashamed to ask for help. I never wanted to burden anyone. I truly believed we could keep fighting on our own, but we can't anymore.

title: My Son Lost an Eye and Part of His Brain… and I'm Afraid He'll Also Lose His Will to Live.
story:
My name is María López and I am the mother of Jesús Moreno, a young man of just 15. I never imagined I would have to write these words to ask for help.

Until recently, my son was a teenager full of dreams. He liked to study, play, go out with his friends, and talk about everything he wanted to do when he grew up. Our life was simple, but we were happy.

Everything changed in a matter of seconds.

A terrible accident nearly took my son away from me forever. For hours, doctors fought to save his life. Thank God he survived, but the consequences were devastating.

Jesús lost one of his eyes and also suffered a severe brain injury that caused him to lose part of his brain. Since that day, our life has never been the same.

Today my son faces challenges no child should ever have to live through.

The neurological aftereffects have caused him to gradually lose mobility. There are days when it's hard for him to walk, hold objects, and even carry out simple tasks. Doctors explained that he needs medication permanently, intensive physical therapy, specialized appointments, and constant rehabilitation to keep him from losing more function and mobility.

As if this weren't enough, the one eye he has left is also losing vision because of the accident's effects. He urgently needs special glasses to try to preserve the little vision he still has.

title: Please Help My Little Girl Smile Again
story:
My name is Susan, and I am Anthee's mother.

I never imagined I would have to ask strangers for help to save my little girl, but today I have no other choice.

Anthee is only 10 years old.

She should be worrying about school, making friends, playing outside, and dreaming about what she wants to be when she grows up. Instead, every single day, she wakes up wondering if people will laugh at her again.

My daughter was born with a rare genetic condition called Crouzon Syndrome, which caused the bones in her skull to fuse much too early. As her brain continued to grow, the pressure forced her eyes outward, changing her appearance and creating serious medical complications.

Watching your child suffer physically is heartbreaking.

Watching her lose her happiness is even worse.

Every day at school, Anthee is bullied because she looks different. Children point at her, whisper, laugh, and call her cruel names. Some refuse to sit next to her. Others stare at her as though she isn't a little girl with feelings.

When we go outside, strangers often stop and stare. Some even reach out and touch her face out of curiosity, without asking, without realizing how deeply it hurts her.

I watch my daughter pretend she's okay...

But when we get home, she cries.

She asks me why she can't look like everyone else.

She asks me why people are so mean.

As a mother, there are no words painful enough to describe those moments.

Over time, the constant bullying has stolen the light from her beautiful smile. The little girl who used to laugh all day has become quiet, withdrawn, and afraid of the world around her.

Today, Anthee is also battling depression. She often begs me not to send her to school because she's terrified of being laughed at again. No ten-year-old child should have to carry that kind of pain.

Her struggles don't end there.

Because of Crouzon Syndrome, she has difficulty breathing, suffers from frequent infections, and cannot fully close her eyes while she sleeps.

Every single night, before I put my daughter to bed, I gently tape her eyelids shut to protect her eyes from drying out and being permanently damaged.

Every night, I kiss her forehead and silently pray that one day she won't have to live like this anymore.

Despite everything, Anthee is still the sweetest little girl. She still dreams of having friends. She still dreams of going to school without fear. She still believes that kindness exists.

There is hope.

A life-changing orbital decompression surgery, costing $20,000, could relieve the pressure around her eyes, protect her vision, improve her breathing, and give her the chance to live a safer, healthier, and more normal life.

Sadly, our family cannot afford this surgery on our own.

That is why I am humbly asking for your help.

Every donation, no matter the amount, brings my daughter one step closer to the life every child deserves—a life without constant pain, without fear, and without being judged simply because she was born different.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you for taking the time to read our story.

Thank you for believing in my little girl.

With love,

Susan

title: Help save Alexa — support her fight against SCA3
story:
Hi, my name is Alexa, and I have a rare disease called SCA3 (Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3). It affects all movement, especially voluntary functions such as speaking, walking, swallowing, seeing, and many others. It is a progressive disease. My symptoms began in 2012, and they have continued to worsen over the years.

I am originally from the United Kingdom and currently live in the United States. I moved here six years ago with my ex-husband and my daughter. Since October 2024, I have had no contact with my daughter whatsoever. There was no mediation from social services. I met the social worker responsible for her case only three times, and it took a tremendous amount of effort to make even those meetings happen. I do not know him well enough to understand why he has not done his job. As a result, I have been completely cut off from my daughter for more than a year and a half, with no way to communicate with her or know how she is doing.

Due to several traumatic events that occurred last year, which I have explained in my videos, my health has been severely affected. Before all of this, I was able to go out by myself, cook, and live an almost normal life.

Now, I need more support. My caregivers only have enough time to prepare meals and help with basic household tasks. I am currently applying for additional caregiving hours for the third time so that I can leave my home accompanied by a helper.

Last year, I became extremely debilitated. Despite everything I was going through emotionally, I also had to be hospitalized multiple times due to complications related to my disease.

I have many expenses, including medical bills, medications, nutritional supplements, rent, and household utilities. I would also like to travel to visit my family in the United Kingdom, but airfare is very expensive, and I would need a caregiver to accompany me on the trip.

I also need a life. Right now, I am only surviving. I live alone in my apartment and am completely isolated from the world—not because I choose to be. This is not loneliness; it is isolation. And isolation has a devastating impact on the brain and emotional well-being.

I need glasses because my eyesight has deteriorated significantly, and I can no longer read comfortably. I also need to purchase a computer because managing my life through a cellphone has become increasingly difficult. My hands shake due to parkinsonism, which is another symptom I deal with daily.

There is currently no cure and no effective treatment for my disease.

I have no support network in the United States. Once or twice a year, an acquaintance may come to visit. People are busy living their own lives, which is understandable. But I, too, need some form of social connection and human interaction.

Today, I am humbly asking for your support. Any donation, no matter how small, will make a meaningful difference in my life.

I will be forever grateful for your kindness and generosity.

Please help me find some relief, peace, and dignity during this difficult journey.

Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

Yours sincerely,
Alexa

story:

It started as something small. Just a wound on her face that we thought would heal. But it didn’t. It kept growing. Slowly at first… and then faster and faster, until in a couple months it became something we could no longer ignore.

Now, that cancer is eating away at her face.

There are moments when she tries to speak, but she can’t. The tumor has taken so much from her already. She spends most of her time lying down, unable to move, unable to live the life she once had.

My mother is a single mother of seven children. After my father passed away, she carried everything on her own. She worked every day just to make sure we had something to eat. She was strong for all of us. She was everything.

And now… she is the one who needs us.

We live in very poor conditions here in Uganda. We don’t have access to proper healthcare, and we have no money for treatment. There are days when we don’t even have food. We are completely alone in this.

We recently went to a hospital, and the doctors told us the truth we were afraid to hear. The cancer is aggressive and spreading fast. Without urgent surgery to remove the tumor, she may not survive.

title: Help Noah Afford Scleral Lenses and Eye Surgery
story:

Simple things other people do without thinking are difficult for me. Reading, walking outside, recognizing faces, cooking, working, getting around safely and living independently all require enormous effort.

This has also caused severe anxiety and depression. The fear of losing more vision, the frustration of depending on others and the loneliness of living in darkness have taken a heavy toll on my mental health.

I have finally found a specialist in New York who may be able to help. I urgently need specialized scleral lenses that could improve my vision and reduce the more than twenty eye drops I use each day, as well as complex surgery on my only functioning eye.

My insurance will not cover these treatments, and the cost reaches six figures. Follow-up appointments are required every six weeks, and I cannot afford them alone. I have held onto the dream of seeing better for 33 years, but every time I get close, it is pulled away again.

I am not asking for luxury. I am asking for the chance to see better, live with greater independence and stop feeling so alone in this fight.

But now I'm watching him suffer, and it's tearing me apart.

He became weak, scared, and disoriented, and I froze because I didn't understand what was happening. I held him in my arms while I cried, repeated his name, and begged him to stay with me.

Every time it happens, I think I'm going to lose him.

The vet told me Ollie has a brain tumor and needs urgent treatment. This cannot wait. Every seizure puts his body through more stress and could cause more brain damage.

The vet also prescribed phenobarbital to help control the seizures, but the cost of the medication, follow-up visits, tests, and treatment is more than I can afford on my own.

If Ollie doesn't get the care he needs soon, the episodes could become more frequent, more violent, and harder for his body to withstand. He could lose even more control, grow weaker, stop eating, have trouble walking, or suffer a seizure so severe that he might not wake up again.

It hurts me so much to know that, after so many years of loving me unconditionally, money could be the reason I'm unable to save him.

I am not ready to lose my best friend. Please help me save Ollie. 🙏🐾💔

title: Help Cassiel fight stage 4 neuroblastoma
story:
My name is Sandra, and I am Cassiel's mom. I am writing this from a hospital chair that has become my bed, my desk, and my prayer bench.

A few months ago, my biggest worry was whether Cassiel would walk before his first birthday. He was still so little — wobbly on his feet, falling after one or two steps, giggling when I caught him. He could not even run. He was just learning what it meant to be a big boy.

Then the screaming started.

He cried like he was being hurt, but I could not find the wound. His tiny belly grew hard and swollen. He stopped wanting his bottle. He stopped smiling. He stopped trying to stand.

Doctor after doctor. ER after ER. Every test came back with the same confused faces — until the scans came back. Stage 4 neuroblastoma. A tumor wrapped around his abdomen. Cancer already spreading through a body that has only been on this earth a short time.

IMAGE:uploads/campaigns/help-cassiel/story-01.jpg|Cassiel during treatment

Those words split my life in half. Before them, I was a mother worrying about diapers, first steps, and lullabies. After them, I became a mother begging strangers to help me save my baby.

Cassiel has already started chemotherapy. He is brave beyond words. But he is still so small. He does not understand why his body hurts. Why nurses wake him up. Why I cry when I think he is asleep.

Neuroblastoma does not give families time. The treatment plan ahead is brutal and expensive: more chemo, possible surgery, stem-cell transplant, radiation, and immunotherapy that can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars.

Insurance helps, but it does not cover everything. It does not cover the trips to the specialist center. It does not cover the hotel rooms when we cannot go home between treatments. It does not cover the experimental options that might become his only hope when standard treatment stops working.

We are not asking for luxury. We are asking for time. Every dollar here buys another day of treatment, another chance for the medicine to work, another week that Cassiel gets to be a baby instead of a patient number.

I have heard people say, 'I only have $20.' To you I say: $20 is medicine. $50 is a meal when I cannot leave his bedside. $100 is gas to get him to the hospital for a scan that decides what happens next. $250 is a night in the room near treatment when he is too weak to travel home.

And if you cannot give, please share. One share reached the person who gave us our first $500. One share might reach the doctor, the survivor, the miracle we are praying for.

Cassiel is still fighting. When he is not in pain, he reaches for my hand. He tries to smile at the nurses. He is still learning to trust a world that keeps hurting him. But he trusts me — and I am asking you, with everything I have, not to let him down.

Please, help us stand with Cassiel. Every donation, every prayer, every share is a step toward healing. One act of kindness really can change everything. It might be the one that saves him. 🙏💛

title: Help Us Save Bruno's Little Face
story:
Hello, we are from Guadalajara, Jalisco, and today I dare to speak up as a mother to ask for the support of this wonderful community to save the health and well-being of my little Bruno.

Exactly one year ago, our lives changed completely when we noticed a vascular tumor appearing on Bruno's face. For those who may not know, a vascular tumor is an abnormal lesion formed by a cluster of blood vessels that grow rapidly and uncontrollably.

Having this type of lesion on the face is a very delicate situation: the risks are very high, as it can cause severe hemorrhaging from any slight friction, affect his vision or breathing as it continues to grow, and compromise the proper development of his features and facial structure.

At first, doctors told us to monitor its progress, but the lesion has advanced rapidly and has now become a critical medical emergency. Specialists have warned us that we have a strictly limited window of 60 days to complete the entire clinical process and perform the surgical procedure before the tumor compromises his health even further.

IMAGE:fh/bruno-2.jpg|

As a single mother, I have tried everything within my power to get ahead and cover my son's medical expenses, but the complexity of this case completely exceeds my means. Bruno urgently needs highly specialized reconstructive surgery and comprehensive treatment that requires a total budget of 550,000 pesos—an amount impossible for me to reach alone and with time working against us.

To provide complete transparency, here is the official breakdown of the medical budget: Urgent medical tests ($45,000 MXN) — MRIs, contrast-enhanced CT scans, and Doppler studies to map the tumor's blood supply. Specialized medical team ($190,000 MXN) — reconstructive plastic surgeon, pediatric oncologist, anesthesiologist, and surgical team. Operating room and technology rental ($130,000 MXN). Hospitalization and care ($95,000 MXN). Medications and supplies ($50,000 MXN). Recovery therapies ($40,000 MXN).

With each passing day, the tumor keeps growing and the window to operate on Bruno becomes smaller. This is not something that can wait until next month or next year: the doctors were clear, and the clock is already ticking.

I am not just asking for a contribution; I am asking you to join this race against time to give Bruno the chance to heal and smile without risk before our time runs out. Every peso goes directly toward the tests, the operating room, and the team that will reconstruct his face.

If you are unable to donate, sharing our campaign on your social media is invaluable support. From the bottom of my heart, thank you for your empathy, your trust, and for helping us save Bruno. God bless you.

— Esmeralda Roa, Bruno's mom

title: Diabetes Supplies for Uninsured Kids
story:
Every month, our clinic sees children whose families are rationing insulin because they can't afford a full monthly supply. In 2026, in the United States, this is still true. We refuse to accept it.

This campaign funds a full year of supplies — insulin, continuous glucose monitors, test strips, and pump supplies — for 30 uninsured or under-insured children with Type 1 diabetes in the Phoenix metro area.

The breakdown per child, per month, is roughly $60 for insulin, $80 for CGM sensors, and $25 for test strips and lancets. Over 12 months across 30 kids, that's about $22,000 — and no family pays a cent.

We've been running this program on a shoestring for three years. Every kid we've enrolled has stayed enrolled. No emergency room visits for DKA. No missed school days for hypoglycemia. It works.

Please help us keep the shelves full. These are literal, life-saving supplies for kids whose only mistake was being born to parents without the right insurance card.

title: Emergency Surgery for Luna
story:
Luna was found on the shoulder of Highway 9 last Tuesday morning. A driver stopped, wrapped her in a hoodie, and drove her straight to our clinic. She couldn't move her back legs, but she was purring. She's still purring.

The X-rays confirmed a spinal fracture consistent with a car strike. Our lead veterinarian consulted with the neurology team at the university hospital, and the consensus is clear: with surgery in the next 10 days, Luna has a strong chance of walking again. Without it, she doesn't.

The estimate is $6,800 all-in: $4,200 for the surgery itself, $1,400 for the two-week inpatient recovery, and $1,200 for the follow-up imaging and physical therapy that gives her the best shot at a full recovery.

Whiskers Rescue is a small operation. We don't have $6,800 sitting in a fund. What we have is a community that has never once let a Luna slip through the cracks — and we're betting on you again.

Even $10 gets us there. Please share this with anyone who loves a cat.

title: Help Ángel beat leukemia and finally have his hands
story:
Hello. I am Ángel's mom, and I want to tell you a little bit about my son.

"Hello, my name is Ángel. I am 8 years old. About eleven months ago, the doctors told me I have lymphoblastic leukemia. I was also born with something called bilateral amelia — I don't have arms. I have never had hands."

He learned to do everything with his feet. Drawing. Writing. Eating. Bathing. Wiping himself in the bathroom. Everything that the rest of the world does without thinking, my son had to figure out how to do — with his feet, all on his own, at 3, at 5, at 8 years old.

And now, on top of that, he is fighting cancer. Every morning is a battle for his body to survive another round of chemotherapy. There are days with fevers. Days with infections. Days when the pain wins and he cries, and there is nothing I can do other than hold him.

IMAGE:fh/angel-2.jpg|

"There are days when I get very sick and days when I can't bear the pain and I cry, but my mom is always here with me. What hurts the most is not being with my brother. He is my best friend, the one who helps me with everything when my mom has to work to bring food home."

We have been living inside this hospital for eleven months. I sleep here, by his side. His older brother is home alone while this happens, waiting for us. The doctors say the treatment will last for years.

This is what I am asking for, honestly and without hiding anything: money for his prosthetic arms and money for hospital expenses that never stop — medications, food, transportation, and the rent that keeps running while I cannot work because I cannot leave my son alone.

This is exactly what your donation achieves: $20 buys the medication that gets him through a bad night. $50 covers a day of food and transportation for both of us here at the hospital. $100 pays for hospital supplies for a week. $250 truly brings us closer to the prosthetic arms he has wanted his entire life.

IMAGE:fh/angel-3.jpg|

"I want a normal life. To run, to jump, to eat everything I can't eat right now and, above all, for the three of us to be together again. Thank you, and I hope I can touch your heart and you can help me with a little bit." ♥️

If you cannot donate, please share this page. That is how strangers found us, and strangers are the only reason we are still standing.

— Áridai, Ángel's mom

title: Help Atticus & Athena start their new life
story:
Atticus, my great-grandson, was born with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome on July 19, 2025 — a heart missing its entire left side.

He has never known a home. Since the day he was born he has been at UF Shands Pediatric Hospital in Gainesville, Florida. He has already survived open heart surgery. The doctors are doing everything they can, but Atticus may still need a heart transplant to live.

His mother, Athena, is our granddaughter. She has not left his side. She lives at the Ronald McDonald House so she can be there every single day, and his father Isaiah works without stopping to keep them afloat. They are 20-something years old, holding a baby's life together in a hospital corridor.

Here is the part that keeps us up at night: when Atticus is finally cleared to leave that hospital, there is nowhere for him to go.

IMAGE:fh/atticus-2.jpg|

They need a safe place to live. They need a bed, a crib, furniture, the basic things that make a room a home. Athena needs a reliable car, because a child with half a heart does not get to miss appointments — the drive to the cardiologist is not optional, it is his life.

This is what your help buys: $20 covers gas for one trip to the hospital. $50 buys essentials for the nursery. $100 goes toward the first month's deposit on a safe apartment. $250 puts real furniture in an empty room so a fragile baby has somewhere to come home to.

We are not asking for luxury. We are asking that after everything this baby has survived, he gets to leave the hospital and go home — to an actual home.

IMAGE:fh/atticus-3.jpg|

If there is anything you can do, it would mean the world. And if you cannot give, please share this page and keep our family in your thoughts. Thank you for reading Atticus's story.

— Atticus's great-grandmother

title: Help Betty Access Life-Saving Cancer Treatment Abroad 🎗️
story:

Betty is fighting stage four neuroblastoma, a rare and aggressive childhood cancer.

We are trying to raise £520,000 for specialist neuroblastoma treatment in Barcelona, Spain. This treatment could give Betty a fighting chance against the cancer.

How can you help? I’m asking for 260,000 people to donate £2 each, then tag 5 friends to donate and keep going until we reach our target. Even if you can't donate, please share our page. If you have the means to donate more, please do.

Betty's Story

IMAGE:fh/betty-2.jpg|

On 9th July we were given the devastating news that Betty had relapsed for a second time, with this news came something much worse.

Betty’s cancer was no longer considered curable and the NHS can now only offer stability. Betty is now considered terminal.

I cannot put my feelings into words. Our hearts have been torn apart as our fiercely strong little girl fights to not give up.

After several conversations, we have discovered a few options we could try, but unfortunately these come at a substantial cost.

I cannot believe we are in a situation where money might be the reason Betty can get the treatment she needs.

As a parent I have to do everything in my power to give her the best chance, I cannot give up nor accept that cancer will take her from us.

Please help give Betty a chance 🎗️

My name is Rochelle, and I am writing this with a broken heart for my sister Charmaine.

My sister is a disabled single mother, and she survived something no woman should ever have to endure. Her ex-husband, the man who was supposed to protect her, set their house on fire with her inside. Charmaine almost died that day. Her little son, Amari, almost lost his mother forever. By the grace of God, she survived, but her life was never the same again.

The fire left her body covered in scars, constant pain, and weakness. She now has only 20% vision in one eye, and every movement, every attempt to care for her son, reminds her of the brutality of what was done to her. I see her looking in the mirror and feeling ashamed of her own face. I see her trying to be strong for Amari, but I know that inside she is broken.

Now we are living in extreme poverty. My sister can no longer work like before. Her body is damaged, her health is fragile, and every day is a battle just to survive. Amari, who is only 2 years old, does not understand why his mommy cries in silence or why there is sometimes not enough food. They depend on my help, but I cannot carry everything alone.

IMAGE:fh/bff-charmaine-2.png|

This is not just poverty. This is a cruel injustice. A man destroyed my sister's life, burned her body, and now she is left fighting alone to survive and raise her son.

We are also fighting for justice. We are seeking help to hold him accountable for what he did, but the process is long, expensive, and emotionally exhausting. While we fight for justice, we are also struggling to survive day by day.

We urgently need help with diapers, food, water, clothes, building materials for a safe roof, medical care, and everything my sister and my nephew need to keep going.

IMAGE:fh/bff-charmaine-3.png|

Please, if God touches your heart, help us. Any donation, no matter how small, can give my sister and Amari a chance to rebuild their lives.

If you cannot donate, please share her story and leave a prayer for them. My sister survived the fire, but now she needs help to survive what came after. 🙏💔

title: Help Colter come home safe and strong
story:
Colter entered the world already fighting for every heartbeat. He was born with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS), a severe congenital condition in which the left ventricle—the chamber that should pump oxygen-rich blood through his body—did not develop.

Instead of spending these first months peacefully at home, his tiny body has faced hospital rooms, monitors, oxygen checks and major surgery. His parents, Daniel and Kiana, have had to watch their baby endure things no child should ever have to understand.

Colter has made it through one enormous battle, but his fight is not over. His family says he is now waiting for another major heart surgery. His oxygen levels and heart rate have returned to normal, giving them precious hope, yet the next operation still stands between this baby and the chance to grow stronger at home.

A hospital stay does not pause the rest of life. While Daniel and Kiana remain close to Colter, the mortgage, insurance, fuel and everyday household costs continue to arrive. They are also trying to prepare his nursery, make essential home repairs and provide everything he will need when doctors finally say he can leave the hospital.

IMAGE:fh/colter-7.jpg|

Even feeding their baby safely has become another worry. The family stores a large supply of breast milk for Colter, but their refrigerator has repeatedly stopped working. They urgently need a dedicated chest freezer so the milk his body depends on is not lost, and they may also need to replace the refrigerator if the problem continues.

No parent should have to choose between sitting beside a baby before heart surgery and earning enough to keep that baby's home secure. Daniel and Kiana did not expect to ask strangers for help, but the weight of prolonged hospital care has become too much for one family to carry alone.

A donation today helps keep their mortgage and insurance paid, puts fuel in the car for hospital journeys, protects Colter's milk supply and prepares a safe nursery for the day he can finally come home. It gives his parents room to focus on the one thing that matters most: helping their son survive and heal.

IMAGE:fh/colter-8.jpg|

Colter has only half a heart, but he is surrounded by people willing to fight for all of it. Please donate if you can. If you cannot, share his story so the next person sees the baby behind the hospital wires and helps carry him toward his next heartbeat, his next surgery and his first safe night at home.

— Daniel and Kiana Rowell, Colter's parents
